answer_raw:
For your specific hardware, **MLX is faster for benchmarks**, but **Ollama is the better choice for agentic workflows** [1].

The comparison isn't symmetric because they serve different purposes: **MLX** is optimized for peak throughput and overnight benchmarks, while **Ollama** is designed for developer experience and serving agents [1]. If you are running autonomous coding agents, use **Ollama**; if you are running pure performance stress tests, use **MLX** [1].

Regarding your capacity, you can realistically run **30B models at full precision** or **70B models with Q4 quantization** [3].

| Model Tier | Quantization / Precision | Feasibility on 48GB M4 Pro |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **30B** | Full Precision | Smooth operation [3] |
| **70B** | Q4 Quantization | Loadable/Usable [3] |
| **70B** | Q6_K | Requires 64GB+ (M4 Max) for daily use [7] |

With 48GB of unified memory, your primary constraint is the split between model weights and the KV cache (context window). A **70B Q4_K_M** model is the practical ceiling for your machine [7]. While you can load larger models, they will likely exceed your available memory once the context window starts to occupy significant space [4].
